question: How can users change their password without re-encrypting all their data, and if the key comes from a passphrase via PBKDF2 for an encrypt-then-MAC scheme, how many bits are derived and how are they used?
answer: Encrypt data with a random key that is itself encrypted with a password-derived key, so only that key is re-encrypted; derive 384 bits via PBKDF2, split into K1 (AES-128-CBC key), K2 (IV), K3 (HMAC-SHA-256 key).
support: the data itself is encrypted with a randomly generated key, which in turn is encrypted with a password-derived one || generate 384 bits of key ... Split these into three 128-bit keys K1, K2 and K3

question: In SQL Server, how can I stop decimal multiplication and division from giving unexpected precision or scale, and what formula gives the result scale of a division before it is capped?
answer: Explicitly CONVERT every operand to a fixed DECIMAL(15,6); the division result scale is max(6, s1 + p2 + 1), and anything above 38 is cut down to 38.
support: tailor the expressions ... by making much more verbose explicit conversions || The result scale for a division is max(6, s1 + p2 + 1)

question: On a Debian-based system the man page for cp is missing, and other commands have no page either. Which dpkg config file edit restores the standard pages, and which man section holds POSIX descriptions of the other commands?
answer: Remove the /usr/share/man and /usr/share/groff lines from /etc/dpkg/dpkg.cfg.d/01_nodoc, then reinstall man-db, manpages and coreutils; the POSIX command pages are in section 1P (POSIX Programmer's Manual).
support: remove the lines matching /usr/share/man and /usr/share/groff from /etc/dpkg/dpkg.cfg.d/01_nodoc || POSIX Programmer's Manual (man section 1P)

question: On a machine with no compiler, how do I install a prebuilt GCC distribution tarball, and what alternative lets me produce executables for that machine from a different architecture?
answer: cd / and run tar xzvf on the tarball, since it is a tarred-up installation image; alternatively cross-compile, building executables for one architecture on a system of a different architecture.
support: a tarred-up installation of GCC. All you need to do is untar it to the root directory || Cross-compiling ... allows you to compile executables for one architecture on a system of a different architecture

question: In bash, how do I pass a wget user-agent option containing spaces from a variable correctly, and what is a safer alternative to eval for filling variables into a stored template string later?
answer: Quote the variable, wget "$user_agent", and keep option lists in arrays expanded as "${arr[@]}"; instead of eval, define a function that assigns the strings, then set variables and call it.
support: in the wget call , "$user_agent" is quoted. This is crucial. || It would be a lot more robust to define a function instead of a string.

question: Besides encrypting traffic, what does a CA-signed web server certificate establish, and which certificate should an ordinary site that is not a bank buy?
answer: It authenticates who owns the website (someone invested in proving ownership); for a non-bank site, get the cheapest certificate, since typical users see no difference if the browser doesn't complain.
support: to authenticate who the owner of the website is || get the cheapest certificate you can

question: In bash, how can I make .* match all hidden files except . and .., and what exactly does the glob .??* match?
answer: Set GLOBIGNORE=".:.." and unset dotglob with shopt -u dotglob; .??* matches a literal dot, any two characters, then zero or more non-slash characters, so at least three characters.
support: use the GLOBIGNORE variable to hide the . and .. directories || matches any file name that begins with a literal dot ., followed by any two (not necessarily the same) characters

question: A script calling ssh-add fails with 'Could not open a connection to your authentication agent'. How do I start an agent for it, and how do I clean it up when the script ends?
answer: Run eval $(ssh-agent) (or ssh-agent -s) to start the agent and export its variables, then ssh-add; at the end of the script run ssh-agent -k, without eval, to kill it.
support: run ssh-agent -k (without eval) at end of script to kill the agent || you can start one and set your environment up thusly eval $(ssh-agent)

question: How many key-derivation iterations does a KeePass database use by default, and what extra step makes a cloud-stored copy of the database harder to breach?
answer: The default is 6000 iterations (12000 AES invocations per password); additionally encrypt the cloud-stored file with a separate key you keep with you, so an attacker needs two compromises.
support: The default number of iterations is 6000 || it requires two points of compromise instead of one

question: Which kinds of executable files need read permission to be run, and what mode on a directory lets people run a known tool inside it by name but not list its contents?
answer: Scripts (and anything handled by binfmt_misc) need read permission, while compiled binaries do not; chmod 711 on the directory lets people run /tools/mytool by name while ls is denied.
support: shell scripts, in fact scripts in general, require read permission, as would any executable handled by binfmt_misc || chmod 711 /tools ... ls /tools/ will be denied

question: How can rsync keep deleted or overwritten files in a separate directory instead of discarding them, and how can I delete from one directory every file that exists at the same relative path in another?
answer: Use rsync --backup with --backup-dir=DIR; for duplicates, cd into the old directory and run find . -type f -exec rm -f ../new/{} \;
support: --backup-dir=DIR ... to keep a copy of any modified and removed files in a separate directory || find . -type f -exec rm -f ../new/{} \;

question: In SQL Server, when does an nvarchar(max) column cause extra I/O, and what fraction of a variable-length column's declared length does the engine assume when sizing sort or hash memory grants?
answer: Values over about 8000 bytes spill out of row into text storage, needing extra I/O; the engine assumes columns average 50% of their declared maximum length for sort/hash memory grants.
support: Larger nvarchar (max) data items (over 8000 bytes or so) will spill over into text storage and require additional I/O || the 50% assumed by SQL Server when calculating sort/hash memory grants

question: Why can ETags make clients re-download the same file from round-robin load-balanced web servers, and how can Tomcat be made to stop sending them?
answer: Each server generates its own ETag, so the client fetches the file repeatedly; in Tomcat, add a filter mapped to the default servlet whose response wrapper drops setHeader calls named etag.
support: each server will generate its own ETag causing the client to grab it multiple times || create a filter for DefaultServlet which swallows the tag

question: ls shows a filename starting with '?', but typing a literal ? doesn't match it. Why, and what are two ways to remove such a file?
answer: ls prints non-printable characters as ?; remove it with a glob such as rm -i ./*ssolve*, or in bash/zsh quote the exact name like rm $'\177' after checking with ls -ld $'\177'.
support: The ls utility will replace non printable characters with ? || First ensure that the name is right with: ls -ld $'\177'

question: Can a nonce-and-hash challenge login work without the server storing a plaintext-equivalent password, and what does LastPass do to the password on the client before sending it?
answer: Yes: algorithms exist that avoid storing plaintext-equivalents on the server. LastPass does many PBKDF2 rounds on the client, then one SHA-256 round, and the server hashes the result again with PBKDF2 and a salt.
support: Yes, this is possible ... avoids the need to store plaintext-equivalents on the server || Many rounds of PBKDF2 on client ... One round of SHA-256

question: In PostgreSQL, how can I build a dynamic cast statement that safely quotes the type name, and how do I write a try_cast-style helper that returns a default on failure?
answer: Cast the type name to regtype and use format() with %L for the value and %s for the type; for try_cast, wrap the cast in a PL/pgSQL BEGIN ... EXCEPTION WHEN others THEN RETURN p_default block.
support: All you need is the cast to regtype || exception when others then return p_default

question: Apache writes its files into a private, hash-named directory under /tmp. What setting causes that, and how can I change it for Apache's unit without editing the package-supplied unit file?
answer: PrivateTmp=yes causes it; run systemctl edit on the service to create a drop-in .conf under /etc/systemd/system/<unit>.service.d/ setting PrivateTmp=no, leaving the upstream unit untouched.
support: PrivateTmp=yes ... desirable to setting PrivateTmp=no || creating .conf files in a drop-in directory /etc/systemd/system/<unit-name>.<unit-type>.d/

question: To find missing numbers in a sequence, which Raku operator takes the non-symmetric set difference of the full range and the numbers seen, and what comparison does awk (splitting on [_.]) use to flag a gap in numbered filenames?
answer: Raku's ASCII (-) (or Unicode ∖) applied to (1..10) and the set of seen numbers; awk with -F'[_.]' flags a gap when $2 != prev+1.
support: ASCII (-) stands for Set difference (non-symmetric) || awk -F'[_.]' ' $2 != prev+1 { print "file " prev+1 " missing" }

question: In Vim in a terminal, how do I map Ctrl-S to save, and what does Ctrl-S do at the terminal level that can interfere, and which key undoes it?
answer: nnoremap <c-s> :w<cr>; but terminals treat Ctrl+S as XOFF flow control (stop transmitting), and Ctrl+Q sends XON to resume.
support: nnoremap <c-s> :w<cr> || XOFF flow control command (Ctrl+S) ... XON flow control command (Ctrl+Q)

question: My web server log shows GET requests mentioning cmd.exe and System.Net.WebClient that returned 404. What do they indicate, and why do people send requests for pages that don't exist?
answer: They are attempted Windows exploits; the 404 means the vulnerable /public/index.php is absent, so no damage. Such probes check whether you are already compromised or try to provoke errors that leak server information.
support: your server does not have the vulnerable /public/index.php file, so no damage was done || looking to see if you are already compromised, or looking to get your server to throw an error
